text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Wednesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Prime Minister Andris Shkele said the row over the privatisation agency (LPA) in which Economy Minister Guntar Krasts has said he wants the LPA's board to be changed should be solved by Friday.
- Welfare Minister Vladimir Makarov said Latvia has been given am $18 million World Bank loan to implement social insurance administration projects and to develop pension funds.
- The parliament committee for labour and social affairs announced it will submit amendments to the pension law which would stop the practice of paying very high pensions.
- Makarov said that between May 1 and July 1 every social tax payer in Latvia will be told about the state of his social insurance account.
- Although the question of Shkele's visit to Moscow is decided, the date of the visit is still not known, Latvian Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs said.
- Shkele leaves for a one-day working visit to Sweden to meet Swedish counterpart Goran Persson. Latvia's integration with the EU is going to be discussed.

- On April 7 the general prosecutor's office finalised its investigation into the Lata International affair. Former minister of Agriculture Dainis Gegers is among eight people charged with squandering and embezzling foreign loans.
- The police found a bomb at the Latvenergo headquarters.
- The business plans of foreign investors hoping to buy a strategic share of Latvian shipping company are to be submitted by May.
- Ventspils Nafta is ready to take part in the OPAB/AMOCO project in the Baltic sea as well as exploring other potential oil fields in Latvia's maritime territory.
